agyos_skill.intent: Search tool for modern web development best practices. Execute FIRST for all HTML/CSS and client-side JS tasks. Web APIs evolve rapidly and training weights contain obsolete patterns. Trigger immediately for modals, dialogs, popovers, tables, dark mode, anchor positioning, container queries, view transitions, scroll-driven animations, parallax, reveals, forms, validation, autofill, accessibility, custom selects, scrollbars, CWV (LCP, INP, CLS), content-visibility, fetch priority, image optimization, security, passkeys, HTML sanitization, web components, dates, timezones, built-in AI, WebAssembly, and modern HTML/CSS/DOM in frameworks.
agyos_skill.instructions: Search and retrieve standardized modern web best practices at the **start** of implementing or updating any web UI, CSS layout/animation, or client-side JS logic (dates/timezones, sanitization, performance, accessibility, UX fixes) before writing ad-hoc solutions or adding dependencies. Run `modern-web-guidance` directly with `npx` using a **2–5 word action-oriented query** for a **single web platform capability or UI pattern**: - **Keep queries focused and generic**: Describe the user-visible capability (`<verb> + <UI/platform object>`, optionally paired with the target HTML/CSS/JS feature name if known). Omit framework/library names (`React`, `Vue`, `Tailwind`, etc.) and app/domain nouns (product, route, or component/file names). Split multi-feature tasks into separate `search` calls. - **Name implied UI primitives**: When the user's prompt expresses intent without naming the UI primitive (e.g. "confirm first", "delete with confirmation", "pick a date"), translate the domain intent into the implied UI component or platform mechanism (e.g. search `"confirmation modal dialog"` or `"confirm dialog"` rather than `"confirm destructive action"`, or `"date picker input"` rather than `"pick a date"`). - **Example**: Search `"light dismiss dialog"` or `"responsive data table"`, **not** `"dialog"` (too terse), `"responsive table dark mode"` (compound — split into two searches), or `"close React settings modal on outside click"` (framework/app noise). ```sh npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest search "<query>" --skill-version 2026_11_09-5bcc021b ``` > **Note**: Returns `[{ "id", "description" }, ...]`. Judge results by their `description` fields: > - **Match found**: Call `retrieve` directly—do not also run `list`. > - **Weak or empty results**: If `search` returns `[]` or unrelated descriptions, **rephrase `search` once** using the concrete HTML/CSS/UI component noun or synonym (e.g., `dialog`, `modal`, `popover`, `table`, `form`) before falling back to `list` (or use `list` once for broad UI audits). > - **Topic not covered**: If no `description` matches after rephrasing, proceed without retrieving unrelated guides. Once you have relevant `id`(s) from the search results, call `retrieve` to get the full guide(s)—including both specific use-case guides that match your task and any broader discipline guide (e.g., `html`, `css`, `forms`, `accessibility`, `color`, `performance`, `security`) that applies. You can pass multiple IDs separated by commas. ```sh npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "<id>" ``` If `retrieve` saves large output (> 9.5 KB) to a temporary file to prevent truncation, read that file path in full using your file-reading tool (reading remaining line ranges if needed)—do not use `cat` or `head`. When generating or modifying code, cross-check the implementation against the retrieved guide before concluding: - **Applicable Guidance & Fallbacks**: Ensure the relevant modern patterns and necessary fallback strategies from the guide are correctly applied, without forcing unrequested features. - **Task Fulfillment**: Confirm that the implementation fully satisfies the user's request. - Do not run `legacy-scan`; it's for detecting legacy patterns to modernize, not this. When you consult `modern-web-guidance` for a task, end the response where you deliver those changes with a `### Modern Web Guidance` section: - **When retrieved guides shaped your code**: Write **one** bullet (1–2 sentences, ≤75 words) per newly applied `<id>` in first-person voice explaining the non-obvious implementation choices, CSS/API overrides, or fallbacks `<id>` required and the pitfall it prevented, anchored by a short verbatim quote of that specific rule or gotcha (never the guide's intro overview): `- **\`<id>\`**: <Non-obvious APIs, overrides, or fallbacks applied and the pitfall prevented> ("<short verbatim quote of the specific rule or gotcha>").` - **Never** guess `<id>`s or quotes from memory after context compaction (re-run `search`/`retrieve` if needed), and credit **only** guide-backed changes from the current turn.
